reason: The flora says the leaves are 'light green to blue-green'. Leaf colour as a range from light green (FLOPO_0988166) to blue green (PATO_0104020) matches it.
The legume is 2-locular, so 2 locules inside the fruit is right.
The dorsal sepal is about 3.2 cm long and 0.7 cm wide, so 3.2 cm is the first number of 'length × width'. Small gaps: 'ca.' (about) and 'dorsal' are not recorded, but the statement is still true.
The sepals are 'barely pubescent outside', so pubescent on the outer (abaxial) surface of the sepal is right. 'Barely' (sparse) is lost, but the annotation stays true.
'Clusters few-flowered' means a few flowers per inflorescence. The annotation keeps the inflorescence as the container and 'few' as the amount.

fix: A side word just before a hair phrase ('abaxially with ... trichomes') limits the phrase to that side. Use the abaxial surface as the bearer, as the 'outside', 'above' and 'beneath' scope rule already does.
reason: The waxy scale-like hairs are on the underside of the blade only. 'Pubescent' on the whole lamina overstates this. The 'mature' stage slot is right.
The scope offset points to the 'apex obtuse' in the Petals clause ('Petals free, yellow, suboblong, 3-4 mm, apex obtuse'), so an obtuse petal apex is right.

fix: In Rosaceae (Potentilla, Fragaria) 'bractlets' are the segments of the epicalyx (outer bracts beside the sepals), not bracteoles on the flower stalk. Map 'bractlets' next to 'sepals' to epicalyx (PO_0009063). Also, 'A and B subequal' is a comparison between A and B.
reason: Here the bractlets are the epicalyx lobes, which are nearly equal in size to the sepals. The 'equal, approximately' value is fine; the bearer class is wrong.

fix: 'Glaucous' is a waxy bloom on the surface, not the colour green. Ground it to glaucous (PATO_0104277), as the 2026-11-14 union-pair reviews already decided.
reason: 'Leaves somewhat glaucous' describes a bloom. The flora does not say the leaves are green.
The involucre is calyculate (it has a calyculus of 3 or 4 bracts). This follows the reviewed rule calyculate → epicalyx present, since calyculus is a PO synonym of epicalyx.
'Leaves shorter than culm': shorter leaf, compared to the stem (culm).

fix: In 'X N-flowered', X is the container. Fill bearer_container with X (a verticillaster is a PO synonym of cyme inflorescence), as A02884 does for 'clusters few-flowered'.
reason: The count of 2-8 flowers is per verticillaster. Without the container it reads as 2-8 flowers per plant, which is false.

fix: Read the 'lobes' after a flower part as perianth or tepal lobes, not leaf lamina lobes. In Thesium, the anthers are joined to the tepals by tufts of hairs.
reason: Anther 'adnate' is what the flora says, but the comparison target PO_0025517 (leaf lamina lobe) is wrong. The anthers are joined to the perianth lobes.

The basal leaf blade is 'elliptic, ovate, or oblanceolate', so the three shape values joined by 'or' match. The blade of the cauline leaves is also elliptic, so leaving out 'basal' does not make it false.

'Follicules généralement nombreux' (French: follicles usually many) means fruits (follicles) present in large number. The words 'généralement' (usually) and 'à maturité' (when mature) are lost, but it stays true.

fix: In 'Sori N rows on each side of midrib', N counts rows, not sori. Treat it as an arrangement (sori in 2 rows on each side of the midrib), not as amount = N of the part.
reason: The flora gives 2 rows of sori on each side, not 2 sori.
'Lucid' (shining) on the leaflet blade, grounded to glistening (glossy).
Petiolules up to 1.5 cm long: a maximum length of 1.5 cm.

fix: Selaginella leaves come in kinds by position (lateral, median, axillary). Keep 'median leaves' in the position slot. The lateral leaves are 0.75-1 mm wide.
reason: The width of 0.35 mm is for the median leaves only. Said of the leaf in general, it is false for the lateral leaves.

fix: In French '... à la base' / 'au sommet' (at the base / at the tip), the shape words before it are about the base or tip of the blade, not the whole blade. Also, 'arrondi' means rounded, not obtuse (PATO_0001935).
reason: 'Arrondi ou légèrement cunéiforme à la base' (rounded or slightly wedge-shaped at the base) describes the base of the leaf blade. The whole blade is elliptic-obovate to elliptic-ovate.
The leaflets are glabrous above, which is the adaxial (upper) surface.
The capsules are roughly longer than the calyx: longer fruit, compared to the calyx, with 'approximately'.
'Graines nombreuses' (French: seeds many): seeds present in large number.

fix: In 'ovaire ..., atténué en style, de N mm de long' (ovary ..., narrowed into the style, N mm long), the measurement right after the style most likely belongs to the style. Cardamine ovaries are longer than 1 mm.
reason: The 1 mm is more likely the length of the style than of the ovary, which grows into a silique 2.5-6 cm long.

fix: 'Apex obtuse or nearly acute' is said of the apex. Scope the bearer to the apex (there is no leaflet apex class; use leaf apex PO_0020137 or a leaflet apex class), as A02886 does.

The carpels are hispid or hirsute. The flora's 'sparsely to densely' amount and its 'rarely glabrous' alternative are dropped, but the values given are true.
